Security scan summary, 2026-04-16 07:07 BST

Host status
- macOS 26.4.1 on Apple Silicon
- OpenClaw stable 2026.4.14, up to date
- OpenClaw audit: 0 critical, 0 warn, 1 info
- `openclaw security audit --fix`: ran clean, no OpenClaw changes needed
- FileVault: ON

- Firewall stealth mode: ON
- Automatic OS update checks: ON
- No pending macOS updates

What I found
- OpenClaw itself is in a good state. It is loopback-bound and the audit came back clean.
- Most listening services are loopback-only.
- Non-loopback listeners seen:
  - `rapportd` on 49153, normal Apple service
  - `next-server` on 3000 from `projects/uk-trade-jobs`, but inbound to Node is blocked by the macOS firewall
  - `limactl` on 53, and inbound to `limactl` is currently permitted by the macOS firewall

Fixes applied
- Tightened `/Users/philsagent/.ssh/config` from 644 to 600
- Tightened `/Users/philsagent/.docker/config.json` from 644 to 600
- Tightened `/Users/philsagent/.docker` from 755 to 700

Deferred item
- `limactl` listening on `*:53` is the only meaningful remaining exposure. I did not auto-block it because that could break Colima/container networking. This needs a deliberate yes/no decision on whether Colima should ever accept inbound LAN traffic.

Could not fully verify
- Time Machine recency, because `tmutil latestbackup` needs Full Disk Access
- macOS Remote Login via `systemsetup`, because it requires admin password, though no `sshd` process was running

Bottom line
- No critical issues found
- 3 safe hardening fixes applied
- 1 medium-risk item remains deferred: Colima `limactl` on port 53
